thread:
alex_dev: FYI seeing sustained P95+ tail blips in eu-west-1 for the large-model pools when prefetch/kvcache warmups kick in. latency climbs for 200-400ms for a small subset of requests, looks capacity-related rather than model quality.

mike_infra: Can you paste the metric window? is this correlated with queue length or GPU memory pressure?

alex_dev: 5m window. spike correlates with a short surge in prefetch jobs that populate long context KV (context>32k tokens). queue depth up ~60% for ~90s, GPU mem shows transient 10% increase — probably copying large KV into GPU which pauses the fastpath.

jasmin_sre: @alex_dev thanks. This smells like admission policy interaction: prefetch tasks are counted same as normal inference for admission credits? If so they may be starving live requests during warmups.

alex_dev: Right now prefetch uses same admit queue token. Proposal: change to hybrid admit policy where prefetch gets a soft quota and a degraded-execution path instead of full admission. That would avoid hard rejects but keep tail latency bounded.

sarah_prod: High level trade-offs: reject=fast failure (clear feedback, client retries cheaper), degrade=serve cheaper/faster model or shorten context (silent correctness risk), queue=holds until capacity (increases latency but preserves quality). For product, silent degrade is risky for ranking/QA flows.

mike_infra: Agree. Operationally I think we need three levers: 1) limit concurrent prefetch jobs per-host, 2) probabilistic degrade for prefetch (drop long-context KV prefetch with X% chance), 3) bounded queue timeout with early reject fallback.

alex_dev: Draft config I sketched for an experiment: 

```yaml
admission:
  mode: hybrid
  prefetch:
    concurrency_limit: 6
    degrade_probability: 0.3  # random soft-drop of expensive prefetches
    degrade_action: truncate_kv_to_8k
  runtime_requests:
    queue_enabled: true
    max_queue_seconds: 3
    reject_after: 5  # hard reject after 5s if still queued
  metrics:
    emit_tags: [prefetch, degrade, queue_reject]
```

jasmin_sre: That looks reasonable. Can we instead have degrade_action be ‘prefetch-on-cold-path’ which warms a lighter-weight cache (summary embeddings) so that correctness impact is measurable? Truncating context is more visible to downstream.

alex_dev: Good call. Update: degrade_action -> prefetch_summary. Will add an eval to measure QA score delta.

deploy-bot: deploy plan created: infra/admit-experiments/prefetch-hybrid v1 -> canary eu-west-1 small-pool (10% traffic) scheduled at 2026-04-02T09:00Z.

mike_infra: Experiment checklist:
- Instrument events: prefetch_started, prefetch_degraded, prefetch_rejected, request_queue_time
- Add trace flags for GPU memory copy ops
- Fallback: if model latency SLO violated -> immediate rollback

alex_dev: I'll own the eval prompts and data slice. Want to track metric deltas: P50,P95,P99 latency, regen rates, QA exact match on our 3 prompt sets, and cost delta.

sarah_prod: Important: notify sales/support about potential transient errors for customers on Dedicated. Add a customer-impact flag in the rollout so we can pause for any enterprise alerts.

jasmin_sre: Oncall note: @oncall please be ready for noisy alerts during canary. We'll have auto-rollback at 2x P95 baseline or error rate >0.5% above baseline.

alex_dev: Quick question — should we keep queue_enabled=true for runtime requests during canary, or test with queue disabled to observe reject vs degrade behavior in isolation?

mike_infra: Start with queue_enabled=true. We want to see combined behavior since that's how prod runs. If metrics look weird we'll flip to queue=false in canary-two.

sarah_prod: Also ensure logs include "admit.reason" tag (prefetch_vs_runtime) so we can separate signals.

jasmin_sre: I'll add observability dashboards and alerting rules. Plan: 1) deploy to canary (10%) 2) 30m burn-in 3) evaluate metrics 4) expand to 50% if ok.

alex_dev: Thanks all. I'll update the PR with modified degrade_action and the eval plan.

mike_infra: :thumbsup:

sarah_prod: :eyes:

deploy-bot: Canary started at 2026-04-02T09:00Z for admit-experiments/prefetch-hybrid v1 (10% traffic)

alex_dev: Leaving this thread open for immediate observations — will post the first evaluation after 30m.
